tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.

Confirmed decisively. Under CI conditions (GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY set, which the harbor suite's own comment documents is true for every step):

- The banner (`TEST FIXTURE — not a real run`) goes to **stdout/log**.
- The fixture report goes to **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY** — the step summary page, i.e., exactly the surface the ticket's evidence quotes — with **no banner**.

So in the environment that motivated the ticket, the banner never appears next to the report. The PR's central mechanism claim ("fixture renders that reach the CI log carry a banner... makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") is incorrect for CI: the pasted chunk from the step summary page carries no banner. Additionally, these tests pollute the real unit-test step's summary page with fake run reports (which is precisely where the false-alarm quote came from).

Also note the mls suite: `test_summary_mls.py` ExitContractTest.run_main → summary_mls.main() → same sink behavior; fixture RUN_CONFIG has `"model": "glm-5.3-flash"` and `provider: daytona` — an unbannered, production-model run identity appended to the CI step summary page, out of guard reach.

Now — how to classify?

**Finding 1: banner/report surface split (BLOCKING).** The fix's mechanism does not work in the target environment; AC #2 ("rendered fixture output in tests should carry a visible banner") is not met for output rendered under CI conditions; the fixture report still lands on the step summary page (the exact false-alarm surface) without any marker. Fix: pop/redirect GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY in these tests (the harbor suite already demonstrates the hermetic pattern) so main() prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`, or write the banner into the sink as well.

**Finding 2: mls_bench masquerade unfixed (IMPORTANT, arguably BLOCKING as ticket-AC gap).** Ticket proposal 1 explicitly names "model names" among production-shaped fixture fields; the mls RUN_CONFIG fixture binds `glm-5.3-flash` and is replayed verbatim into the rendered run identity, unbannered, and the guard can't see it (no run-label carrier on the line; the `"model":` dict key isn't in `_RUN_LABEL_CARRIERS`). Synthetic value is feasible here — this fixture doesn't key into pricing.json (need to confirm mls has no pricing use... summary_mls renders no cost column keyed by model? The terminal render shows "est cost" with $0.000 — that's terminal's. For mls, the model is only replayed as identity text). So feasibility holds. I'll rate this IMPORTANT... but is it an AC gap = scope violation = BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING includes "scope violations". The ticket AC says "the same rule for any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: model names, run URLs, task ids **where feasible**". The mls model fixture is feasible to change and renders a production model identity into CI-visible output — the same sin at a smaller scale. I think this deserves BLOCKING too... but let me be careful about over-blocking. The machine protocol says "When in doubt, start one level higher."

Hmm. Consider the intent: the ticket's false-alarm was caused by the Provider line. After this PR, terminal_bench and harbor fixtures are synthetic; mls still emits `- model: glm-5.3-flash` into the step summary page in CI. A future reader could quote that as "CI shows an mls run with glm-5.3-flash" — the same class of false alarm. The guard that is this PR's durable prevention explicitly scans all three roots but structurally cannot catch this. Given the ticket explicitly listed model names and the PR left a live instance, I'll mark it BLOCKING? 

Let me think about grader/rework economics: marking 2 BLOCKINGs means REQUEST_CHANGES. Both are real and actionable. Finding 1 is solid (mechanism factually doesn't work in CI). Finding 2 is a genuine remaining instance of the exact bug class, in-scope per the ticket text. I'll keep both BLOCKING... Actually, let me reconsider finding 2's severity once more. The PR description says: "Guard scope: production tokens (zai-glm, kimi-for-coding) on any non-assertion line bound to a run-label carrier... Resolve-step provider-name inputs and pricing.json-key model fixtures are intentionally out of scope... and documented in the guard's docstring." The mls fixture is neither a resolve-step input nor a pricing.json key — the documented exclusions don't cover it, so it's an undocumented scope gap rather than a justified exclusion. The rendered mls report includes the model in the run-identity header — exactly a "rendered run identity". Yes: BLOCKING is defensible... but hmm, one could argue mls render is a different report and the ticket evidence was terminal-bench. The ticket title: "Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs" — bench-wide. The guard scans all three roots. I'll go BLOCKING for finding 2 as well? 

Let me weigh: the instruction says "When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible." The risk of finding 2 is not negligible (same false-alarm class, live instance, guard can't catch). Keep BLOCKING.

**Finding 3: guard evasion via indirection (SUGESTION or IMPORTANT).** Same-line heuristic: `_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"` at module level, then `run_label=_LABEL` — combined-label rule catches the constant line? The constant line `_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"` contains the combined run label → caught by rule 2 (combined label outside assertion). But `run_label=_LABEL` line: carrier yes, token no → passes. And a token-only constant like `_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"` + `BENCH_RUN_LABEL: _PROVIDER`... the dict line contains carrier + no token → evades. So indirection via constants evades. It's a heuristic guard; noting as IMPORTANT? The guard is the durable prevention; a one-line-evasion undermines it. But realistically, the guard's docstring acknowledges scope limits. I'd rate SUGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. I'll say IMPORTANT? Hmm — "IMPORTANT — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge." A guard that trivialy evades is a correctness issue in the guard. But the guard is defense-in-depth; the primary fix is synthetic labels + banner. I'll rate SUGESTION... Actually the same-line check is the guard's core design; anyone adding a fixture with an intermediate variable defeats it silently. I'll make it SUGESTION with a concrete suggestion (also scan for module-level constants whose value contains a production token AND is referenced from a carrier line, or simpler: flag any non-assertion line containing a production token assigned to a name — too broad). Keep it SUGESTION.

**Finding 4: typo `caries` (SUGESTION).**

**Finding 5?** The banner test name typo — same as 4.

Another check: `FixtureBannerTest` asserts banner is first line of buffered stdout — fine.

Anything about the guard skipping comment lines: a fixture assignment can't be in a comment. Fine.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

- 🚨 Banner/report surface split in CI — the exact surface quoted by the ticket (step summary page) still receives unbannered fixture reports (and the tests pollute the real step summary file)
- 🚨 mls_bench `RUN_CONFIG["model"] = "glm-5.3-flash"` — in-scope per the ticket's "model names" clause, feasible to synthesize, guard can't see it

## Review summary — PR #1678 (gh-1677)

The PR's core idea is right — synthetic fixture labels plus a durable guard test — and I verified the guard actually works (mutation test: reintroducing `zai-glm-5.3-flash` makes it fail; file restored afterwards, tree clean). All three suites pass except the pre-existing `test_fa_usage` `harbor`-package import error (environment-only, unrelated to the diff).

But two blocking defects remain:

1. **🚨 Banner/report surface split in CI** (`test_summary_1392.py:43`): I reproduced this — with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` set (true for every Actions step, as this repo's own harbor tests document), `summary.main()` writes the full unbannered fixture report to the step-summary file while `_fixture_output()`'s banner goes only to stdout. The banner never appears next to the render it marks — on the very page the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source — and the tests keep appending fake run reports to the real step summary. Fix: pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests (the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses).

2. **🚨 Live masquerade instance left in mls_bench**: `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` still binds `"model": "glm-5.3-flash"` in `RUN_CONFIG`, rendered verbatim as run identity by `summary_mls.main()` into CI output, unbannered — out of the guard's carrier-only reach, and not covered by the documented exclusions (not a resolve-step input, not a pricing key). In scope per the ticket's "model names" clause and feasible to synthesize.

Plus two suggestions: the guard's same-line heuristic is evadable via intermediate constants, and a typo (`caries` → `carries`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1678
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1678
- **Title**: gh-1677 [GOAL] Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs: synthetic labels + fixture banner + guard test
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1677` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +373
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:06:30Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T23:18:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #1677
### What changed

Bench test fixtures can no longer masquerade as production run reports: run-label fixtures now use a synthetic value, fixture renders that reach the CI log carry a `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` banner, and a guard test fails on any future production provider string bound to a run-label carrier.

### Key decisions

- `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` / `run_label=` fixture values are now `test-fixture-provider (fixture-model)` in both `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` and the harbor sibling `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` (the harbor test had the identical sin).
- Banner via a `_fixture_output()` context manager around the `summary.main()` calls — the CI unit-test step runs unittest without `--buffer`, so test stdout lands verbatim in the step log; the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying. Zero production-code change (`summary.py` plumbing untouched).
- Guard scope: production tokens (`zai-glm`, `kimi-for-coding`) on any non-assertion line bound to a run-label carrier, plus the combined label `zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` outside assertions. Resolve-step provider-name inputs and `pricing.json`-key model fixtures are intentionally out of scope (they test the real mapping/pricing contract, not a rendered run identity) and documented in the guard's docstring.

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench
```

All three suites pass (the one `test_fa_usage` import error is pre-existing: this sandbox lacks the `harbor` pip package that CI installs; verified identical on the pristine tree).

# PR Diff Truncated

Original size: 21925 characters.
Kept: first 7800 and last 4200 characters.

The full diff is available in the checked-out PR branch. Use `git diff` or CodeGraph for focused source navigation instead of relying only on this file.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.

## Review summary — PR #1678 (gh-1677)

The PR's core idea is right — synthetic fixture labels plus a durable guard test — and I verified the guard actually works (mutation test: reintroducing `zai-glm-5.3-flash` makes it fail; file restored afterwards, tree clean). All three suites pass except the pre-existing `test_fa_usage` `harbor`-package import error (environment-only, unrelated to the diff).

But two blocking defects remain:

1. **🚨 Banner/report surface split in CI** (`test_summary_1392.py:43`): I reproduced this — with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` set (true for every Actions step, as this repo's own harbor tests document), `summary.main()` writes the full unbannered fixture report to the step-summary file while `_fixture_output()`'s banner goes only to stdout. The banner never appears next to the render it marks — on the very page the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source — and the tests keep appending fake run reports to the real step summary. Fix: pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests (the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses).

2. **🚨 Live masquerade instance left in mls_bench**: `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` still binds `"model": "glm-5.3-flash"` in `RUN_CONFIG`, rendered verbatim as run identity by `summary_mls.main()` into CI output, unbannered — out of the guard's carrier-only reach, and not covered by the documented exclusions (not a resolve-step input, not a pricing key). In scope per the ticket's "model names" clause and feasible to synthesize.

Plus two suggestions: the guard's same-line heuristic is evadable via intermediate constants, and a typo (`caries` → `carries`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1678
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1678
- **Title**: gh-1677 [GOAL] Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs: synthetic labels + fixture banner + guard test
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1677` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +373
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:06:30Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T23:18:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #1677
### What changed

Bench test fixtures can no longer masquerade as production run reports: run-label fixtures now use a synthetic value, fixture renders that reach the CI log carry a `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` banner, and a guard test fails on any future production provider string bound to a run-label carrier.

### Key decisions

- `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` / `run_label=` fixture values are now `test-fixture-provider (fixture-model)` in both `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` and the harbor sibling `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` (the harbor test had the identical sin).
- Banner via a `_fixture_output()` context manager around the `summary.main()` calls — the CI unit-test step runs unittest without `--buffer`, so test stdout lands verbatim in the step log; the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying. Zero production-code change (`summary.py` plumbing untouched).
- Guard scope: production tokens (`zai-glm`, `kimi-for-coding`) on any non-assertion line bound to a run-label carrier, plus the combined label `zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` outside assertions. Resolve-step provider-name inputs and `pricing.json`-key model fixtures are intentionally out of scope (they test the real mapping/pricing contract, not a rendered run identity) and documented in the guard's docstring.

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench
```

All three suites pass (the one `test_fa_usage` import error is pre-existing: this sandbox lacks the `harbor` pip package that CI installs; verified identical on the pristine tree).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1678._

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 9 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: typo in test name — `caries` → `carries`**

`test_rendered_fixture_output_caries_the_banner` should be `test_rendered_fixture_output_carries_the_banner` ("carries"). The misspelling makes the test slightly harder to find when grepping for "carries" and will fossilize into muscle memory. Rename before merge costs nothing.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed. `_fixture_output()` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` (lines 44–60) now pops `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` for the block and restores it on exit, so `summary.main()` prints the fixture report to stdout — under the banner — exactly like the hermetic `setUp` pattern in `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py`. Both `summary.main()` call sites (`test_main_reads_env_tag`, `test_main_reads_env_label`) run inside the manager.

A regression test reproduces your exact repro: `FixtureBannerTest.test_main_render_stays_on_the_banner_surface` exports `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` pointing at a temp file, runs `summary.main()` inside `_fixture_output()`, and asserts the report starts with the banner on stdout and the sink file is never created.

Verified under simulated CI conditions (`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` exported for the whole run): after all three discovery suites, the sink file does not exist — no unbannered fixture report reaches the step-summary page anymore.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed. `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` now uses `"model": "fixture-model"` in `RUN_CONFIG` (line 81, with a comment citing gh-1677), and `ExitContractTest.run_main` wraps `summary_mls.main()` in a `_fixture_output()` manager (same contract as terminal_bench: banner on stdout, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` popped and restored).

The guard in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fixture_hygiene.py` was extended with rule 3: a production token (`zai-glm`, `kimi-for-coding`) or model token (`glm-5.3`) in a run-config identity key (`"model"`, `"provider"`) on a non-assertion line is a violation, unless the line carries a contract payload (`apiKeyEnvVar`/`baseUrl`/`"role"`/`"usage"` — the documented resolve/pricing exemptions). Pinned by `GuardRuleTest.test_intermediate_constant_is_caught`.

The assertion exemption was also tightened as suggested: only lines *starting* with `assert` / `self.assert` / `with self.assert` are exempt, so a trailing comment merely mentioning "assert" can no longer launder a fixture line — pinned by `GuardRuleTest.test_assert_word_in_trailing_comment_does_not_launder`.

# gh-1677: [GOAL] Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs: synthetic labels + fixture banner + guard test

## Description

### Problem

The bench summary's unit-test fixture is indistinguishable from a real run report:

```
fa on terminal-bench

Provider: zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash) (gh-1471).
0/1 resolved — accuracy 0%
Failure families (mode x resolved):
...
```

This is the "Unit-test bench scripts" CI step output (job step summary page) — `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py:330` sets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL=zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` as the test fixture, and the rendered fixture output is byte-shaped exactly like a production summary. Anyone reading CI logs reasonably concludes the model label is hardcoded (this already cost one full false-alarm investigation today: a real kimi-for-coding run was suspected of being a glm run because of this output).

The production plumbing itself is correct — `summary.py` renders `Provider:` only from the `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` env, set by bench.yml/bench-harbor.yml's resolve step from the dispatch `provider` input (kimi-for-coding → `run_label="kimi-for-coding"`). There is no hardcoded fallback. The confusion is entirely the fixture masquerading as production data.

### Proposal

1. **Synthetic fixture labels**: test fixtures must use obviously-synthetic values, never production-looking ones — e.g. `BENCH_RUN_LABEL=test-fixture-provider (fixture-model)` (and the same rule for any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: model names, run URLs, task ids where feasible).
2. **Fixture marker**: rendered fixture output in tests should carry a visible `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` banner line, so a pasted/quoted chunk can never be mistaken for CI truth.
3. **Guard test**: a test asserting no bench test file contains a production provider/model string (`zai-glm`, `glm-5.3`, `kimi-for-coding` etc. as fixture VALUES — referencing them in assertions about plumbing is fine, assigning them as fixture data is not).

### Evidence

- Fixture: `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py:330`.
- Real run header for comparison (run 39028127116, kimi-for-coding): the step summary shows `Provider: kimi-for-coding` — correct — but the adjacent unit-test step output shows the zai fixture, which is what gets noticed and quoted.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1678
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1678
- **Title**: gh-1677 [GOAL] Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs: synthetic labels + fixture banner + guard test
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1677` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +373
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T18:06:30Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T23:18:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #1677
### What changed

Bench test fixtures can no longer masquerade as production run reports: run-label fixtures now use a synthetic value, fixture renders that reach the CI log carry a `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` banner, and a guard test fails on any future production provider string bound to a run-label carrier.

### Key decisions

- `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` / `run_label=` fixture values are now `test-fixture-provider (fixture-model)` in both `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` and the harbor sibling `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` (the harbor test had the identical sin).
- Banner via a `_fixture_output()` context manager around the `summary.main()` calls — the CI unit-test step runs unittest without `--buffer`, so test stdout lands verbatim in the step log; the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying. Zero production-code change (`summary.py` plumbing untouched).
- Guard scope: production tokens (`zai-glm`, `kimi-for-coding`) on any non-assertion line bound to a run-label carrier, plus the combined label `zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` outside assertions. Resolve-step provider-name inputs and `pricing.json`-key model fixtures are intentionally out of scope (they test the real mapping/pricing contract, not a rendered run identity) and documented in the guard's docstring.

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench
```

All three suites pass (the one `test_fa_usage` import error is pre-existing: this sandbox lacks the `harbor` pip package that CI installs; verified identical on the pristine tree).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1678._

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 9 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: In CI the banner and the report land on two different surfaces — the banner never appears next to the fixture render it is meant to mark**

`summary.py` routes its output to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever that env var is set (summary.py:879-882) and only prints to stdout otherwise. In GitHub Actions CI, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exported for **every** step — this is already documented in this repo's own `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` setUp comment ("CI exports GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for EVERY step, and summary.py prefers that sink over stdout when set — the first revision of these tests failed on real Actions runners").

So in the exact environment that motivated gh-1677, the mechanism splits in two:

- `_fixture_output()` prints `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` → **stdout / step log**
- `summary.main()` writes the full fixture report (`### fa on terminal-bench … Provider: …`) → **$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY / step summary page — with no banner**

I reproduced this locally by running `test_main_reads_env_tag` with `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/sink.md`: stdout got only the two detached banner lines; the sink file got two complete fake run reports, no banner. The step summary page is precisely the surface the ticket quotes as the false-alarm source ("job step summary page") — a pasted chunk from it still carries no marker, so the PR's core claim ("the banner makes any pasted chunk self-identifying") does not hold under CI conditions. Worse, these two tests keep appending fake run reports to the real unit-test step's summary page.

Fix (matches the hermetic pattern `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py` already uses): pop/redirect `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in these tests' setUp so `summary.main()` prints to stdout inside `_fixture_output()`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._sink_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    self.addCleanup(self._restore_sink)
```

(alternatively, write the banner into the sink file too when it is set). The `FixtureBannerTest` can't catch this because it mocks `sys.stdout` and never exercises the sink branch.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the guard only watches run-label carriers — the live `glm-5.3-flash` fixture in `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` renders a production run identity and slips through**

The ticket's proposal item 1 explicitly extends the synthetic-value rule to "any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: **model names**, run URLs, task ids where feasible". One such live instance remains, out of the guard's reach:

- `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py:52` — module-level fixture `RUN_CONFIG = {…, "model": "glm-5.3-flash", …}`
- `ExitContractTest.run_main` calls `summary_mls.main()`, which renders the run-identity block verbatim (`summary_mls.py:142`: `- model: \`glm-5.3-flash\` (fa commit …)`) into CI-visible output — under CI conditions it is appended to the unit-test step's `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMARY` page, unbannered (the `_fixture_output` banner only exists in `test_summary_1392.py`).

The guard structurally cannot catch this: the line `"model": "glm-5.3-flash",` contains neither `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` nor `run_label`, and no documented exclusion applies — it is not a resolve-step provider-name input and not a `pricing.json` key (nothing in `summary_mls.py` prices by model; `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` is only replayed as identity text), so a synthetic value is plainly feasible here.

Fix: give `RUN_CONFIG["model"]` an obviously-synthetic value (e.g. `fixture-model`), banner the `summary_mls.main()` calls in `ExitContractTest`, and extend the guard so a production token in any run-identity carrier (`"model"`, `"provider"` in a run-config fixture, `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`, `run_label`) is caught — otherwise the guard gives a false sense of bench-wide coverage while the same masquerade sin persists in the third discovery root the PR itself lists as in scope.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the guard's same-line heuristic is trivially evadable via an intermediate constant**

`_violations` only flags a line when a carrier substring and a production token appear **on the same line**. Indirection defeats it silently:

```python
_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"   # caught today (combined label)…
run_label = _LABEL                              # …but run_label=_LABEL alone passes
_PROVIDER = "zai-glm"                           # never caught: no carrier on this line
os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _PROVIDER       # evades: token not on this line
```

Since this guard is the PR's durable prevention mechanism, consider one cheap hardening: also flag any non-assertion, non-comment line that *assigns* a bare production token to an identifier (e.g. matches `^[A-Z_]+ *= *["']zai-glm`), or track module-level string constants containing tokens and report any carrier line referencing those names. Not merge-blocking — the primary synthetic-label fix stands on its own.

Relatedly (even smaller): the `"assert" in line` exemption matches the substring anywhere, so a fixture assignment mentioning the word "assert" in a trailing comment would be skipped; checking `stripped.startswith(("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert"))` would tighten it.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: typo in test name — `caries` → `carries`**

`test_rendered_fixture_output_caries_the_banner` should be `test_rendered_fixture_output_carries_the_banner` ("carries"). The misspelling makes the test slightly harder to find when grepping for "carries" and will fossilize into muscle memory. Rename before merge costs nothing.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed. `_fixture_output()` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py` (lines 44–60) now pops `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` for the block and restores it on exit, so `summary.main()` prints the fixture report to stdout — under the banner — exactly like the hermetic `setUp` pattern in `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py`. Verified under simulated CI conditions (`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` exported for the whole run): after all three discovery suites, the sink file does not exist — no unbannered fixture report reaches the step-summary page anymore.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed. `bench/mls_bench/test_summary_mls.py` now uses `"model": "fixture-model"` in `RUN_CONFIG` (line 81, with a comment citing gh-1677), and `ExitContractTest.run_main` wraps `summary_mls.main()` in a `_fixture_output()` manager (same contract as terminal_bench: banner on stdout, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` popped and restored).

Applied both hardenings. The guard now has rule 4: a bare production provider token assigned to *any* identifier on a non-assertion line is flagged (regex on `NAME = "zai-glm…"`), closing the intermediate-constant indirection (`_PROVIDER = "zai-glm-4.5"` → hit). # gh-1677: [GOAL] Bench summary fixtures must never masquerade as production runs: synthetic labels + fixture banner + guard test

## Description

### Problem

The bench summary's unit-test fixture is indistinguishable from a real run report:

```
fa on terminal-bench

Provider: zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash) (gh-1471).
0/1 resolved — accuracy 0%
Failure families (mode x resolved):
...
```

This is the "Unit-test bench scripts" CI step output (job step summary page) — `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py:330` sets `BENCH_RUN_LABEL=zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` as the test fixture, and the rendered fixture output is byte-shaped exactly like a production summary. Anyone reading CI logs reasonably concludes the model label is hardcoded (this already cost one full false-alarm investigation today: a real kimi-for-coding run was suspected of being a glm run because of this output).

The production plumbing itself is correct — `summary.py` renders `Provider:` only from the `BENCH_RUN_LABEL` env, set by bench.yml/bench-harbor.yml's resolve step from the dispatch `provider` input (kimi-for-coding → `run_label="kimi-for-coding"`). There is no hardcoded fallback. The confusion is entirely the fixture masquerading as production data.

### Proposal

1. **Synthetic fixture labels**: test fixtures must use obviously-synthetic values, never production-looking ones — e.g. `BENCH_RUN_LABEL=test-fixture-provider (fixture-model)` (and the same rule for any other production-shaped field in bench fixtures: model names, run URLs, task ids where feasible).
2. **Fixture marker**: rendered fixture output in tests should carry a visible `TEST FIXTURE — not a real run` banner line, so a pasted/quoted chunk can never be mistaken for CI truth.
3. **Guard test**: a test asserting no bench test file contains a production provider/model string (`zai-glm`, `glm-5.3`, `kimi-for-coding` etc. as fixture VALUES — referencing them in assertions about plumbing is fine, assigning them as fixture data is not).

### Evidence

- Fixture: `bench/terminal_bench/test_summary_1392.py:330`.
- Real run header for comparison (run 39028127116, kimi-for-coding): the step summary shows `Provider: kimi-for-coding` — correct — but the adjacent unit-test step output shows the zai fixture, which is what gets noticed and quoted.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gh-1677: bench test fixtures must never masquerade as production runs.

The unit-test step runs `unittest discover` WITHOUT --buffer, so anything
a test prints lands verbatim in the CI step log next to real run
summaries. A fixture that binds a production provider string to a
run-label carrier (BENCH_RUN_LABEL env, run_label= kwarg) renders a
report byte-shaped like a real run and has already been mistaken for one
(a real kimi-for-coding run was suspected of being a glm run because the
fixture's `Provider: zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)` line was quoted
from the unit-test step's log).

Guard rules, scanned over every bench test file (all three CI discovery
roots):

1. A production provider token (zai-glm, kimi-for-coding) may never be
   bound to a run-label carrier on a non-assertion line — assigning it
   as fixture data is the sin; referencing it in an assertion about the
   resolve-step plumbing is fine.
2. The combined production run label 'zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)'
   may appear only on assertion lines (the resolve-mapping contract).
3. A production run identity — a provider token (zai-glm,
   kimi-for-coding) or a production model token (glm-5.3) — may never
   sit in a run-config fixture's identity key ("model", "provider") on
   a non-assertion line: those keys replay verbatim into the
   CI-visible report. Exempt: the same line carrying a contract
   payload — provider-config JSON (apiKeyEnvVar/baseUrl) or an
   assistant usage record ("role"/"usage") — which exercises the real
   mapping/pricing contract, not a rendered run identity.
4. A bare production provider token assigned to ANY identifier on a
   non-assertion line is flagged: the same-line carrier heuristic is
   otherwise evadable via an intermediate constant
   (_LABEL = "zai-glm-..."; os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = _LABEL).

Assertion exemption: only lines STARTING with an assert statement are
exempt — a trailing comment merely mentioning "assert" must not
launder a fixture line.

Out of scope by design: model-id fixtures that must reference a
bench/pricing.json key (pricing/usage math tests) and the resolve-step
tests' provider-name INPUTS — those exercise the real provider mapping,
not a rendered run identity.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
"""
import re
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

_BENCH_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
_DISCOVERY_ROOTS = ("terminal_bench", "harbor_fa", "mls_bench")

_PRODUCTION_TOKENS = ("zai-glm", "kimi-for-coding")
_PRODUCTION_MODEL_TOKENS = ("glm-5.3",)
_RUN_LABEL_CARRIERS = ("BENCH_RUN_LABEL", "run_label")
# gh-1677 review round 2: run-identity keys of a run-config fixture
# (the mls RUN_CONFIG dict) — replayed verbatim into the CI-visible
# report, so a production value there is the masquerade sin on a
# carrier the run-label rules cannot see.
_RUN_IDENTITY_KEYS = ('"model"', '"provider"')
_COMBINED_RUN_LABEL = "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)"
# A line carrying one of these markers is a contract payload
# (provider-config JSON / assistant usage record), not a rendered run
# identity — the resolve-step inputs and pricing.json-key fixtures the
# docstring documents as out of scope.
_CONTRACT_FIXTURE_MARKERS = ("apiKeyEnvVar", "baseUrl", '"role"', '"usage"')
_ASSERT_PREFIXES = ("assert", "self.assert", "with self.assert")


def _test_files():
    files = []
    for root in _DISCOVERY_ROOTS:
        files.extend(sorted((_BENCH_DIR / root).glob("test_*.py")))
    # The guard file itself carries the banned strings as its rules'
    # data — never a fixture.
    return [p for p in files if p.resolve() != Path(__file__).resolve()]


def _violations(path: Path) -> list:
    """(lineno, line, rule) for every fixture-as-production binding."""
    hits = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if stripped.startswith(_ASSERT_PREFIXES):
            # Assertions ABOUT the plumbing may reference the real
            # strings; only assignments as fixture data are banned.
            # startswith, not substring: a trailing comment merely
            # mentioning "assert" must not launder a fixture line.
            continue
        if _COMBINED_RUN_LABEL in line:
            hits.append(
                (lineno, line, "combined production run label outside an assertion")
            )
            continue
        providers = [t for t in _PRODUCTION_TOKENS if t in line]
        models = [t for t in _PRODUCTION_MODEL_TOKENS if t in line]
        carriers = [c for c in _RUN_LABEL_CARRIERS if c in line]
        if carriers and providers:
            hits.append(
                (
                    lineno,
                    line,
                    "production provider string bound to a run-label carrier as fixture data",
                )
            )
            continue
        if any(k in line for k in _RUN_IDENTITY_KEYS) and (providers or models):
            if not any(m in line for m in _CONTRACT_FIXTURE_MARKERS):
                hits.append(
                    (
                        lineno,
                        line,
                        "production run identity in a run-config fixture",
                    )
                )
                continue
        assign = re.match(
            r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*=\s*(?P<q>[\"'])(?P<val>.*?)(?P=q)", stripped
        )
        if providers and assign:
            hits.append(
                (
                    lineno,
                    line,
                    "production provider string assigned to a constant",
                )
            )
    return hits


class FixtureHygieneGuardTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """gh-1677: no bench fixture may render as a production run identity."""

    def test_no_fixture_binds_a_production_provider_string(self):
        failures = []
        for path in _test_files():
            for lineno, line, rule in _violations(path):
                failures.append(f"{path.name}:{lineno}: {rule}: {line.strip()}")
        self.assertEqual(failures, [])


class GuardRuleTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The guard's own heuristics, pinned against synthetic corpora."""

    def _scan(self, text):
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        path = Path(tmp.name) / "test_fake.py"
        path.write_text(text)
        return _violations(path)

    def test_run_identity_key_flags_a_production_model(self):
        # Review thread 2: a run-config fixture's identity key
        # ("model"/"provider") replays verbatim into the CI-visible
        # report — a production value there is the same masquerade sin
        # on a carrier the run-label rules cannot see.
        hits = self._scan('RUN_CONFIG = {"model": "glm-5.3-flash"}\n')
        self.assertEqual(len(hits), 1)

    def test_contract_payload_stays_exempt(self):
        # A provider-config JSON payload (apiKeyEnvVar/baseUrl) or an
        # assistant usage-record ("role"/"usage") exercises the real
        # mapping/pricing contract, not a rendered run identity.
        text = (
            'CFG = \'{"baseUrl":"https://x","model":"glm-5.3-flash",'
            '"apiKeyEnvVar":"K"}\'\n'
            'REC = {"message": {"role": "assistant", "model": '
            '"glm-5.3-flash", "usage": {}}}\n'
        )
        self.assertEqual(self._scan(text), [])

    def test_intermediate_constant_is_caught(self):
